notes.meaning: David declares that the Lord owns the entire earth and everything in it. Every land, creature, and person belongs to him because he is the Creator. No corner of the world is outside his royal authority.

God's ownership of the world rests on the fact that he made it in the beginning. He set the dry land firmly above the ocean waters and keeps it steady by his great power. Human life stands secure only because the Lord holds creation together.

The psalm asks who is fit to climb the holy mountain and enter the presence of God. This points to the sanctuary in Jerusalem, but it also points upward to heaven itself. The question calls every worshipper to stop and examine their own heart before coming near to God.

The Lord welcomes those whose outer actions and inner desires are clean. Clean hands mean doing what is right and not hurting others, while a pure heart means genuine love and loyalty toward God. Such worshippers do not worship worthless idols or make false promises to cheat their neighbors.

The person who approaches God with an honest heart receives blessing and righteousness from him. Righteousness means being declared right and forgiven by God, which is a gift of his saving grace. All our goodness and reward come entirely from the Lord's mercy.

These faithful worshippers are the true people of God who seek him with their whole hearts. Seeking God's face means seeking his presence, favor, and loving friendship. The musical pause at the end of the line invites worshippers to pause and reflect on this truth.

The singers call on the ancient gates of the city to open wide so the King of glory may enter. In David's day, this pictured the ark of the covenant, the sacred symbol of God's presence, being carried into Jerusalem. Christians also see here a picture of Jesus returning to heaven in triumph after dying and rising again.

The gatekeepers ask who this glorious ruler is, and the royal choir answers with a shout of praise. He is the Lord, all-powerful and victorious over every enemy. His past victories show that no power can ever stand against him.

The call to open the gates is repeated to show how important and joyful the King's arrival is. Repeating the command helps awaken sleepy hearts to welcome God with great awe. It urges God's people to receive their King without any delay.

The gatekeepers ask once more who this King is, leading to the grand title that finishes the psalm. He is the Lord of hosts, the ruler who commands all the armies of angels and the powers of heaven. His people can live with complete peace because their King rules the whole universe.
